steps.narration: ESC-Net begins by taking an input image alongside a set of candidate class text descriptions.
Pre-trained CLIP vision and language encoders process the inputs to extract image and text representations.
The extracted vision feature map and language feature vectors are paired for correlation modeling.
A vision-language correlation step computes cosine similarity across spatial coordinates for each class.
The correlation maps and features are progressively refined through N consecutive ESC Blocks.
Inside each block, the correlation map stack enters the Pseudo Prompt Generator.
The generator thresholds and clusters candidate object locations across the image.
This creates pseudo point coordinates and mask prompts, which are supplied alongside the vision features into the SAM Block.
The SAM transformer block applies prompt self-attention and bidirectional cross-attention to refine the spatial context.
The SAM transformer block applies prompt self-attention and bidirectional cross-attention to refine the spatial context.
The enhanced visual features, along with text features and the original correlation map, are passed to the Vision-Language Fusion module.
The Vision-Language Fusion block sequentially applies image and text guidance to remodel class interactions.
This outputs a multimodally refined correlation map for all candidate classes.
A mask prediction decoder then upsamples the refined features.
The pipeline begins in the first section with multiple camera views and their corresponding foreground object masks.
These inputs are used to construct an initial set of three-dimensional Gaussians containing the statue.
Depth maps are then rendered across the set of camera viewpoints.
Entering the depth-guided mask inference stage, reference and secondary views are paired with their respective masks.
Applying these masks isolates the visible background regions for both viewpoints.
Using depth from the second view, background content is projected onto the reference view.
This determines the final depth-guided inpainting mask for the reference view.
The mask is transferred into the final inpainting-guided refinement stage.
Inpainting is performed on the reference view to synthesize missing background color and depth.
Depth-guided projection then lifts the inpainted reference view into a three-dimensional surface structure.
This structure initializes the refined Gaussians while projecting background information onto the remaining viewpoints.
Finally, render loss on the reference view and cross-view loss on other rendered views supervise the refined scene.
The pipeline begins with the data filtering and cleaning stage.
First, tweets tagged within the Los Angeles geographic area are collected.
The collected tweets are then filtered specifically for COVID-19 keywords.
Next, text pre-processing prepares the tweet corpus for downstream extraction.
The cleaned text passes into the entity and relation extraction stage.
Sentiment analysis computes sentiment scores for tweets and specific keywords.
Topic modeling via matrix and tensor factorizations extracts latent topics and tracks their temporal evolution.
Time series analysis identifies tweet volume peaks and significant sentiment change points linked to real-world events.
Word embeddings evaluate semantic similarity to generate weighted edges between tweets and topic keywords.
These extracted entities and relations are integrated during graph construction.
Definite entities and relations are formalized across tweets, topics, and dates.
Graph queries and visual inspection allow validation of the interconnected structure.
Graph embedding techniques then project the network structure into dense vector spaces.
Finally, the constructed network undergoes in-depth graph analysis.
Community detection identifies tightly coupled clusters of topics and discussions.
Node similarity metrics assess topological and semantic closeness between entities.
Lastly, link prediction infers unobserved associations between events, dates, and topics.
